item.title: Trump says he sees no reason to escalate war with Iran
item.description:
What to know about the Iran war today: In a 60 Minutes interview that aired Sunday, President Trump said he does not currently see "any reason" to escalate the war with Iran. However, he defended starting the conflict as "historically" a good decision, despite its economic impact.Mr. Trump is meeting Monday with the prime minister of Qatar, whose country has mediated indirect talks between the U.S. and Iran aimed at reaching a deal.Secretary of State Marco Rubio curbed expectations late Sunday, saying talks are not "at the verge of a breakthrough" because Iran's demands are "unacceptable"

Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth said he's not worried about a vote on articles of impeachment that could happen in the House as early as this week.

item.title: France says Iran behind costly grocery store refrigeration hacks
item.description:
French officials believe Iran was behind nationwide cyberattacks on commercial refrigeration units at hundreds of grocery stores in October, the Paris prosecutor's office said Monday, accusing a cyber unit of Iran's powerful Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps of carrying out the costly hacks.
The Oct. 11 hacking attack struck major supermarket chains, hitting "700 retail locations across France," according to the prosecutor's office, which said the attack caused "significant food spoilage and triggered roughly twenty fires" as the temperatures in refrigeration units shot up.
The attacks on the French grocery store chains were followed weeks later by similar hacks affecting refrigerators and freezers at supermarkets in Belgium, Luxembourg and Sweden. A separate cyberattack targeted several blood banks in France, but the products and samples were not damaged.
In August, refrigeration outages at six U.S. military bases sparked an ongoing investigation by the Department of the Army Criminal Investigation Division, Thomas Hamilton, a public affairs officer for the department, told CBS News.
There has been no assertion yet by officials in France, the U.S. or the other European nations hit by the hacks that all of the incidents were connected.
In its statement Monday, the Paris public prosecutor's office said its cybercrime division had opened a judicial investigation on charges including "fraudulent interference with an automated data-processing system and causing damage by means dangerous to persons — both committed as part of an organized group."
View of the closed frozen food aisle at a supermarket near Nantes after a cyberattack targeted refrigeration systems at French supermarket chains, causing food losses and fires at several stores, France, Oct. 12, 2026.
Stephane Mahe/REUTERS

item.title: "Forever cruise" ship held on arrest warrant at Singapore port
item.description:
The Odyssey, the "forever cruise" left stranded in Southeast Asia after its owner struggled with financial problems, has been held by authorities in Singapore, according to court records obtained by CBS News.
A Singaporean law firm, Helmsman LLC, is listed as the solicitor in the "arrest" of the ship, but it is unclear whom the firm is representing. A source familiar with the matter told CBS News it is likely a fuel supplier.
"The vessel has been placed under arrest pursuant to a court order," Singapore's Maritime and Port Authority said in a statement cited by the French news agency AFP and other outlets on Monday. "The crew onboard are reported to be well, and arrangements for their welfare and wellbeing are being managed by the vessel's creditors. There are no passengers on board."
It added that the ship was "anchored in Singapore port waters." AFP described the ship as being "impounded" by Singaporean authorities.
The luxury cruise ship is currently being operated by its lender after its owner, Villa Vie Residences, couldn't keep up with payments.
Villa Vie owes one supplier in the area approximately $500,000, though it's unclear whether that supplier hired the law firm to solicit the arrest.
A ship arrest is a legal process in Singapore in which a vessel can be detained or seized following a legal claim.
The journey of the MV Odyssey luxury cruise ship, launched in October 2024, came to a sudden end last month in Cambodia, where residents on the ship had just hours to disembark.
According to accounts from multiple sources familiar with the final weeks on board, these details included a scramble to find fuel while stuck at a port in Singapore, a rush by the crew to obtain provisions once food shipments had ended, and the temporary detainment of the ship in Hong Kong.

item.title: Russell Brand sentenced to over 10 years for rape and sex assault
item.description:
Disgraced actor Russell Brand was sentenced Monday to 10 and a half years in prison for raping a woman in 2009 and sexually assaulting three others.
The disgraced British television personality and Hollywood actor was convicted last week on one count of rape and three counts of sexual assault, but acquitted on two other counts of rape and an attempted indecent assault charge.
A jury of eight men and four women in Southwark Crown Court, in South London, found Brand guilty of groping a woman's breasts at a London bar in 2004, sexually assaulting a woman at a London radio station in 2004 and 2005, and raping a woman at his west London home in 2009.
The judge, Joel Bennathan, called Brand a "sexual predator" in his sentencing remarks, saying he displayed "staggering arrogance" and believed that "fame meant you could act ⁠how you liked, when you liked."
For the rape he was sentenced to nine years, plus 18 months for the sexual assaults. Brand is expected to serve at least seven years in prison, and the rest of his sentence under heavy restrictions, such as wearing a tag.
Six women made the allegations against him, spanning from 1999 to 2009.
Russell Brand outside Southwark Crown Court in London on Nov. 4, 2026.
James Manning/PA Images via Getty Images
Before the sentencing Monday, victim impact statements from the women involved in Brand's crimes were read out in court, three by the prosecutor and one by one of the women, who was hidden from everyone but the judge by a screen.
"I've been in shock and turmoil for years. I was extremely upset and traumatized. I didn't have any respect for myself," the woman reading her statement said, according to CBS News partner network BBC.

item.title: Alleged cartel leader wanted by the U.S. is captured in Mexico
item.description:
Mexican authorities announced on Sunday the arrest of a powerful cartel's regional leader who is wanted by the U.S.
The arrested suspect was identified as Rafael Alvarez, alias "R2," who headed a Jalisco New Generation Cartel (CJNG) cell linked to homicides, drug trafficking and extortion of avocado industry entrepreneurs.
The CJNG was designated a "foreign terrorist organization" by the American government in 2025 and is known for its violent tactics and attacks on authorities.
It competes with the Sinaloa Cartel for drug trafficking into the United States, but since the death of its founder, Nemesio "El Mencho" Oseguera, in a military operation in February, several of its top leaders have been apprehended.
The drug gang operates in the states of Jalisco and Michoacan.
Alvarez is also linked to the killing a year ago of Carlos Manzo, a popular mayor known for the way he confronted organized crime.
Mexico's navy released an image of Alvarez on social media after his arrest.
En Zapopan, Jalisco, personal de la Armada de México, a través de la Unidad de Operaciones Especiales de #Marina, en coordinación con @SSPCMexico, detuvo a Rafael “N”, alias “R2”, identificado como líder de “Los Rs”, célula del CJNG, y presuntamente vinculado con el homicidio de… pic.twitter.com/UATDaaauhk— SEMAR México (@SEMAR_mx) November 8, 2026
The kingpin was wounded in a shootout that broke out during the operation to capture him and is receiving medical care, Mexico's Security Secretary Omar Garcia Harfuch said on X. Another 19 people were arrested along with Alvarez, he said.
The trafficker was located thanks to information shared by the US Drug Enforcement Administration (DEA), Harfuch added.

item.title: Man who carried out mass shooting in Poland has died, police say
item.description:
The 24-year-old who opened fire in a busy city square in Poland, killing six people and wounding 15 on Saturday, died in a hospital Monday morning, police said.
The attacker, who has only been identified as a Polish man, was wearing military-style clothing and a bulletproof vest when he drove into the Main Square in Krakow's Old Town and opened fire. The location is a major tourist destination in Poland's second-largest city, and several foreigners were among the dead and wounded.
Police said the man initially continued firing even after he was wounded by police officers. He had been in critical condition since the attack and had been operated on multiple times. He died at 4:30 a.m. in the hospital, authorities said.
"We are first of all investigating if he was inspired by anyone, if someone helped him," Eryk Stasielak from the Krakow branch of the national prosecutor's office told The Associated Press. "We have secured his electronic devices and we will try to open them and get to the contents."
Poland was in the second of two days of national mourning on Monday.
Investigators recovered nearly a dozen firearms from both scenes. Poland's interior minister initially said over the weekend that the gunman held possible far-right extremist views, but authorities backtracked Monday, declining to offer any possible motive.
"We do not have findings that we could, in a responsible way, categorically state that he was inspired by any particular ideology," national prosecutor's office spokesman Przemyslaw Nowak told reporters.
Prosecutors on Sunday announced the beginning of an investigation into the murder and attempted murder of numerous people, including police officers, saying the act constituted "a terrorist offense."

item.title: Dozens of migrants dead on boats in Europe, scores rescued
item.description:
Greek authorities recovered 13 bodies from a boat carrying migrants found sailing south of the Greek island of Crete early Monday, while one of 18 other people rescued from the same vessel was later confirmed dead at a health center in Crete, the coast guard said.
There was no immediate information available on the identities or nationalities of those on board or what had caused the deaths of the 14 people.
Hellenic (Greek) coast guard members transferring bodies of migrants, recovered from a boat off the island along with survivors, at the port of Agia Galini on the Greek island of Crete on Nov. 9, 2026.
Stefanos Rapanis / REUTERS
In addition, French news agency AFP reports that eight bodies were found on a second boat off Crete and about 28 survivors from that boat, all Sudanese nationals, were picked up by another boat sailing nearby, then transferred to a police vessel and taken to Crete, authorities said Sunday.
Maritime police had launched an emergency rescue late Saturday after a boat issued an alarm signal, with strong winds making sea conditions difficult, the coast guard said.
Two Sudanese citizens, one of them 16, were arrested after being identified by the survivors as suspected people smugglers, authorities said.
Separately, the coast guard said more than 180 other people were found on three other boats heading across the Mediterranean Sea from North Africa to Crete on Monday morning, the latest in what has been a steady number of boats traveling from Libya to Greece. The crossing has become one of the main migrant routes to Europe.
